Joseph Rende.emailSource: Town of North Castle official Town Board roster, Members table (northcastleny.gov)
Joseph Rende.bio: Joseph A. Rende (Joe Rende) is the Democratic Town Supervisor of North Castle, NY (serving Armonk, Banksville and North White Plains), in office since January 2024 after narrowly defeating Republican Councilwoman Barbara DiGiacinto by roughly three votes in a contested, recount-and-litigation election. Professionally he is Director of Business Development at Judicial Title Insurance Agency; earlier he ran and operated his family's home heating oil business, Rende Economy Fuel, alongside his father before selling it to Robison Oil and taking a management role there. Raised in and long a resident of Port Chester, he began his public service in that village's government (planning commission, chairman of the village planning board, elected trustee, deputy mayor) and later served as Westchester County's deputy director of emergency planning and management. He has lived in Armonk for more than ten years with his partner, the Hon. Linda S. Jamieson, a Justice of the Westchester Supreme Court. As Supervisor he has emphasized public safety, fiscal responsibility, and collaborative, cost-saving problem-solving (e.g., organizing local business partners to restore the vandalized North Castle Eagle landmark at no cost to the town), and is running for re-election.

keyIssues: Public safety and police staffing (swearing in officers, reaching budgeted staffing levels, backing the chief)
Grants and capital projects that fund town improvements without burdening taxpayers
Fiscal responsibility and disciplined budgeting (taxes, finance)
Open government, transparent procedure and proper process (heightened sensitivity post-contested election)
Legal, litigation and contract matters affecting the town
Land use, zoning and special permits balanced against fiscal and community interests
engagement.likes: He responds warmly to proposals that strengthen public safety and to well-funded capital and grant-backed projects that deliver visible improvements at little or no cost to taxpayers. He values professionalism, competence, and collaborative, solution-oriented partnerships (including public-private cooperation), and readily gives credit and ceremonial recognition to those who deliver results.
engagement.dislikes: His engagement cools notably on procedural, legal/contract, and land-use/zoning matters, where his sentiment is measured rather than enthusiastic; he is wary of anything that looks fiscally loose, procedurally irregular, or that would raise taxes. Given the disputed nature of his election, he is especially attentive to transparency and correct process, and skeptical of items that appear rushed or cut corners.
engagement.recommendation: Lead with fiscal discipline and a clear public benefit: show how the proposal costs the town little or nothing, ideally leveraging grants, private capital, or partnership, and quantify the upside. Respect process meticulously, arrive with complete, well-documented materials and a transparent record, and pre-empt procedural or legal-review concerns before they are raised, since he dislikes surprises on those fronts. Frame land-use and zoning asks around community benefit, public safety, and orderly process rather than developer convenience, and acknowledge staff and board contributions, collaborative, professional presenters who make him look like an effective, prudent steward earn his support most reliably.

Joseph Rende.notes: Identity is well-corroborated across multiple independent sources (town website, campaign site, The Examiner, CBS New York, Inside Press) with a consistent North Castle/Armonk nexus, so no significant name-collision risk. Email jrende@northcastleny.com was surfaced via the town's official staff directory listing; the directory page itself routes contact through a web form, so the exact address could not be visually confirmed on-page (WebFetch to town/campaign pages returned HTTP 403) and should be verified before use, though it fits the town's first-initial+lastname@northcastleny.com convention. Engagement analysis is grounded primarily in the first-party meeting brief (avg sentiment 0.515; strongest positive engagement on public safety/police 0.669 and grants/capital projects 0.655; more measured on open government/procedure 0.276, legal/contracts 0.315, and land use/zoning 0.365), supplemented by public positions on fiscal responsibility and collaborative problem-solving.

Barbara DiGiacinto.emailSource: Town of North Castle official Town Board roster, Members table (northcastleny.gov)
Barbara DiGiacinto.bio: Barbara W. DiGiacinto is a Republican Councilwoman on the North Castle Town Board, first elected in 2013/seated 2014 and completing roughly twelve years of service as of 2025; she is the board's only councilwoman and has served as Deputy Supervisor. She is a retired English teacher, having taught for about 35 years at Westlake High School. Her family has lived in North Castle for over a century, and she is deeply tied to the North White Plains hamlet, where she kept a 2013 campaign pledge by launching regular North White Plains resident gatherings. Before the Town Board she was treasurer of the North Castle Historical Society and was appointed Chair of the North Castle Housing Board by Supervisor Jack Lombardi. She is a breast-cancer survivor and in 2025 ran for Town Supervisor against Democrat Joseph Rende in an exceptionally close, recount-level race.

keyIssues: Open government, transparency and procedural fairness (frequent dissenting voice on 'rushed' or closed-door processes)
Fiscal discipline: budgets, taxes, AAA bond rating and fund balance
North White Plains representation and neighborhood equity within the town
Water and road infrastructure (Water District 1 rehabilitation, main breaks, brown-water, fire safety)
Open-space and historic preservation (e.g., Miller Hill-contiguous parcels)
Ceremonial recognition and community/civic life
engagement.likes: She responds strongly to proposals framed around civic stewardship, historic and open-space preservation ('our one chance to do the right thing'), and tangible resident quality-of-life benefits such as reliable water and safe roads. Community-honoring and ceremonial gestures, and initiatives serving underrepresented neighborhoods like North White Plains, earn her warmest support. She rewards well-documented, technically justified infrastructure investments and will personally champion and move such items.
engagement.dislikes: She is skeptical of processes she perceives as rushed, opaque, or shutting out residents, and is the board's most reliable dissenting vote when transparency or public access is lacking (e.g., her lone dissent on the Town Hall RFEI over limited document access and timing). She distrusts decisions made before the public has had a chance to weigh in and pushes back on procedural shortcuts.
engagement.recommendation: Bring her fully documented, technically grounded materials well ahead of any vote, and make the public-process history explicit: show what notice was given, what residents were told, and when. Pre-empt transparency concerns by volunteering the record rather than waiting to be asked, and never let her feel rushed. Emphasize fiscal prudence, preservation value, and concrete quality-of-life benefits, and pay particular attention to impacts on North White Plains. Expect and respect probing procedural questions; treating her as the credibility check rather than an obstacle will earn cooperation even when she is in the minority.

Barbara DiGiacinto.notes: Identity is well-established as the North Castle official via multiple town-nexus sources (official staff directory plus repeated local Examiner/Yonkers Times coverage); low name-collision risk. ASR variants Digiacinto/Digacinto refer to the same person (correct spelling DiGiacinto; middle initial W.). Email bdigiacinto@northcastleny.com was surfaced from the official town directory listing and matches the town's naming convention, but the directory page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch, so it is corroborated via search snippet and its appearance in town documents rather than a direct page read; treat as high-but-not-independently-refetched confidence. Tenure (~12 years, seated 2014) and the 35-year Westlake High School teaching career are from local news profiles. Party affiliation is Republican; she served as Deputy Supervisor and ran for Supervisor in 2025.

Saleem Hussain.bio: Saleem Hussain is a Democratic member of the North Castle (Armonk, NY) Town Board, first appointed and then elected as Councilman, and designated Deputy Supervisor for 2026. Professionally he is a longtime IBM executive based at the company's Armonk headquarters, where he has worked for roughly a decade-plus in strategy and AI-focused research/ecosystem partnership leadership roles; multiple aggregator profiles list his title around head of AI partnerships and business development at IBM Research. His reported education includes an MBA from the MIT Sloan School of Management and executive-education study at Stanford Graduate School of Business. On the board he founded and leads the town's Technology Task Force, driving resident communications, data-security upgrades, and digital engagement, and he routinely recuses himself from matters touching IBM to avoid conflicts of interest. He is engaged in civic and community life, championing the public library, parks and recreation, and the town's 250th anniversary of American Independence celebration.

keyIssues: Open government, transparency and improved resident communications (his Technology Task Force portfolio)
Municipal technology, cybersecurity and data protection
Grants and capital projects, and the town budget/finances
Parks, recreation, trails and the public library
Civic identity and commemoration (e.g., America's 250th anniversary planning)
Careful, conflict-aware handling of land use / special permits (measured, not reflexive)
engagement.likes: He responds well to proposals framed around good process, transparency, and clear public benefit, and is notably positive on grants/capital projects, sound budgeting, and parks/recreation and library-style community enrichment. He values leadership and culture that mentors others and 'leans into dissent,' so he rewards openness to feedback and genuine community engagement over a hard sell.
engagement.dislikes: He is markedly more reserved and critical on land use, zoning and special-permit matters (his lowest-sentiment theme) and on legal/litigation/contract questions, signaling skepticism toward dense or aggressive development and toward anything that looks procedurally thin or legally exposed. Opacity, weak public-communication plans, or proposals that skip community input tend to draw his concern.
engagement.recommendation: Lead with process and transparency: bring a clear, well-documented record, an explicit public-communications and engagement plan, and evidence of community benefit (fit with parks/rec, library, or town identity where relevant). Because zoning/special-permit density is his most guarded area, pre-empt concerns with concrete data on scale, impacts, and mitigations rather than conclusory assurances, and respect the board's procedure and hearing steps. Frame asks around measurable public value and long-term stewardship, invite his feedback rather than pushing for a quick vote, and be aware he recuses on IBM-related matters.

Town nexus is solid: North Castle Town Board councilman, IBM employee in Armonk, founder of the town Technology Task Force. Jose Berra.bio: José L. Berra is a longtime Armonk resident (25+ years) serving as a Councilman on the North Castle Town Board, where he was designated Deputy Supervisor for 2024-25. Professionally he is a CPA and tax attorney with a background in investment banking; earlier in his career he worked as a tax lawyer in the Office of Tax Policy at the U.S. Department of the Treasury in Washington, D.C. He was first appointed to the Town Board in January 2014 to fill the seat vacated when Michael Schiliro became Supervisor; after narrowly losing a 2014 special election, he won election in 2015 and has since served multiple full terms, running as an endorsed independent/Democratic-backed candidate. He is a community volunteer with local civic ties including involvement in the Armonk Outdoor Art Show, and on the board has focused on fiscal stewardship, sustainability, and responsible land use.

keyIssues: Fiscal discipline and tax fairness (skeptical of condo tax treatment that shifts burden off developers onto residents)
Legal, contract and litigation diligence (his highest-volume engagement area)
Land use and high-density development scrutiny (development must benefit the town, not just the developer)
Environmental sustainability (food-scrap composting, solar on municipal facilities, open-space preservation)
Grants and capital projects (pool/recreation improvements, county-partnered initiatives)
Open government and clean procedure
engagement.likes: Responds warmly to environmental and sustainability initiatives and open-space preservation (his most positive themes), championing efforts like the food-scrap composting program and the digital Natural Resources Inventory map. He supports well-documented, grant-funded capital projects and proposals framed around concrete resident benefit, and readily praises competent staff and committee work delivered transparently.
engagement.dislikes: Turns skeptical on high-density development and land-use requests that read as developer-favorable with thin public benefit (his lowest-sentiment theme), and on tax structures like condo-style treatment that shorts town revenue. He scrutinizes legal, contract, and budget exposure closely and is wary of proposals that increase fiscal or litigation risk to the town.
engagement.recommendation: Lead with rigorous, CPA-grade financials and a clear-eyed tax/revenue analysis, and bring clean contract and legal terms since these are the areas he examines most. Quantify the concrete benefit to North Castle residents (not just the applicant) and pre-empt density, tax-abatement, and fiscal-risk concerns before he raises them. Where possible, align the proposal with sustainability, open-space, or grant-leveraged public improvements, and respect a transparent, well-papered process, giving him the documentation to reach a confident yes.

Jose Berra.notes: Email jberra@northcastleny.com reported from the town's official staff directory (EID=53) and consistent with the town's first-initial+lastname pattern; the directory page itself returned 403 to automated fetching, so it was confirmed via search-indexed content rather than a live page render. Professional/biographical detail draws on local reporting (The Examiner, Armonk Daily Voice); exact current investment-banking employer and education institutions were not individually verified.

Matt Milim.bio: Matt Milim (Matthew Milim; occasionally misspelled 'Milam') is a North Castle Town Board Councilman and an Armonk, NY resident and finance executive. He earned a BA in Applied Economics and Management from Cornell University and spent roughly 15 years in New York City as an investment analyst and then portfolio manager of a ~$2.5B long-short equity book at a large hedge fund. In 2018 he founded Probate Advance, which grew into a leading inheritance-advance firm, and in 2023 he became CEO of Libra Solutions, where he consolidated several businesses and restructured the company's capital structure. A first-time candidate, he won a surprise victory in the November 2021 Town Board race, finishing ahead of two incumbents despite running with no support from the local Republican committee (later described as independent), and took office in 2022. Locally he serves as Police Department liaison, is President of the Armonk Lions Club, is active on community events (Fol-de-Rol committee, a candlelight vigil for Israeli hostage families, Jewish American Heritage Month recognition), and has recused himself from votes where he had a Lions Club conflict.

keyIssues: Fiscal discipline and capital funding strategy (funding major projects from fund balance vs. bonding; lifecycle cost analysis)
Parks and recreation capital investment and grants (championed the ~$4.1M IBM Community Park artificial turf field)
Public safety and police support (serves as PD liaison; backs appointments and honors service)
Skepticism of for-profit energy/infrastructure proposals that shift risk onto the town (e.g., BESS battery storage)
Data-driven, resident-demand-backed decision making (survey rankings, financial modeling)
Open government and sound procedure
engagement.likes: Proposals grounded in hard data and financial rigor win his support: resident-survey evidence of demand, lifecycle/total-cost-of-ownership economics, and fiscally responsible funding (he argued fund balance, not bonding, was the right source for the turf field). He responds well to clear community benefit, public-safety improvements, and long-requested resident quality-of-life fixes such as targeted traffic/parking changes.
engagement.dislikes: He is deeply skeptical of for-profit ventures where the town bears the risk with little local benefit, exemplified by his strong opposition to the Catalyze Energy BESS project ('I don't see a path... the town wearing all the risk'). He is wary of financing choices that add unnecessary debt when reserves are appropriate, and of proposals that lack demonstrated municipal upside.
engagement.recommendation: Lead with numbers: bring a defensible financial model, lifecycle/total-cost analysis, and evidence of resident demand, since Milim's hedge-fund background means he will probe the economics closely. Frame the clear, quantifiable benefit to the town and be explicit and honest about risk allocation and funding source, pre-empting any perception that the town is absorbing risk for a private party's profit. Respect process and come prepared for peer-review-level scrutiny; where public safety or recreation/community benefit is genuine, foreground it, as those themes consistently earn his enthusiastic support.

Sonny Vataj.emailSource: Town of North Castle official Town Board roster, Members table (northcastleny.gov)
Sonny Vataj.bio: Sonny Vataj (the name is rendered 'Vitaj/Vitage' in meeting transcripts) is a first-term member of the North Castle Town Board, elected in November 2025 (running on the Democratic and Conservative lines) and sworn in for a term beginning January 2026. By profession he is a real estate broker and owner — principal of EXIT Realty Group, servicing the Bronx, Westchester and Putnam markets for close to two decades. The son of an immigrant, he moved to North Castle from the Bronx with his family in 2004, is married and a father of four, and has been a longtime Armonk volunteer firefighter. As a first-time candidate and small-business owner he campaigned on fiscal stability, strategic phased infrastructure investment without tax increases, and a deliberate, resident-involved approach to the Town Hall building decision. He has since been appointed to the town's Revolutionary War 250 Steering Committee.

keyIssues: Value-for-money on capital purchases — spending should match the quality of the asset
Proper board process: no pre-arranging or pre-committing purchases before board approval
Fiscal discipline and strategic, phased infrastructure investment without raising taxes
Resident voice and genuine public participation in town decisions
Data-driven local lawmaking (e.g., verifying the actual scale of short-term rentals)
Personnel, appointments, and recognition of well-vetted staff work
engagement.likes: He responds well to proposals that are thoroughly vetted and backed by concrete data, openly thanking staff for well-prepared work and offering to move or second such motions. He rewards value-for-money and fiscally responsible, phased investment, and he places real weight on demonstrated resident input ('your voice really matters').
engagement.dislikes: He is skeptical of budget/spending items that feel like poor value — memorably objecting to cheap storage containers next to a high-quality park ('You've built a Ferrari in that field and you're asking to go buy used tires') — and he reacted sharply to staff pre-arranging a purchase before the board had approved it. He is cautious on tax and budget matters and dislikes rushed decisions.
engagement.recommendation: Come prepared with hard numbers and evidence that the proposal has been properly vetted, and make clear that no commitments were made ahead of board authorization — respecting board process is a hot button for him. Frame requests around value-for-money and fiscal responsibility (matching spend to the quality and priority of the asset, phased where possible, mindful of tax impact), and show that residents were consulted. Pre-empt his procurement and process concerns explicitly rather than waiting for him to raise them; as a broker and small-business owner he will scrutinize cost-benefit closely.
